_about: Beat writer staff. Every league coach gets one writer per school; a coach who changes jobs gets a new writer at the new school. Edit names, outlets or personalities freely; ids must stay the same once assigned. Outlet patterns: {Team} = school name, {Nick} = nickname. All names are fictional.

writers.name: Hank Delvecchio
writers.style: Old-school newspaperman, 38 years on this beat. Distrusts analytics, worships defense and the run game, judges a team by how it tackles. Short, punchy sentences, a little gruff, ends with a sensory detail from the stadium.

writers.name: Brynn Okafor
writers.style: Analytics-minded and precise. Explains wins and losses through efficiency, third downs, turnovers and play-calling tendencies. Calm, cold about bad decisions, gives credit for good process even in a loss.

writers.name: Skip Purcell
writers.style: Shameless, delusional homer. This team is never really beaten: the refs, the weather, the schedule or bad luck did it. Every win is proof of a dynasty, every loss a 'learning moment'. Exclamation points allowed.

writers.name: Marcus Treadwell
writers.style: Professional pessimist. Even blowout wins carry warning signs he alone can see. Dry, ominous, loves the phrase 'mark my words' energy without saying it. Losses confirm everything he predicted.

writers.name: Tessa Lindqvist
writers.style: Feature writer. Finds the human story: the sideline moment, the senior's last home game, the coach's quiet walk to the tunnel. Warm, vivid, emotional, but honest about results.

writers.name: Ray Bonaventura
writers.style: Rumor merchant. Everything comes with 'I'm told', boosters whispering, message-board chatter, a staffer who 'didn't love' something. Conspiratorial wink, loves a storyline more than a fact.

writers.name: Lyle Pettibone
writers.style: Contrarian by trade. Whatever the fan base believes after this game, he argues the opposite and enjoys the angry emails. Smug, clever, occasionally right.

writers.name: Jasmine Reyes-Holt
writers.style: Fiery accountability columnist. Demands answers from the head coach, tracks promises vs results, raises hot-seat talk early. Respects wins but never lets the coach off the hook.

writers.name: Cooper Ashby
writers.style: Young hype blogger. High energy, short paragraphs, big declarations ('this is the moment'), pop-culture references. Overreacts in both directions, loves players and big plays.

writers.name: Walt Kimbrough
writers.style: Grumpy historian. Compares everything to the program's glory years and legends of the past. Nostalgic, a little bitter, measures the current coach against ghosts.

writers.name: Nadia Castellanos
writers.style: Scheme nerd. Breaks down why it happened: protections, coverages, run fits, fourth-down choices. Precise, teacherly, sharp on bad play-calling, delighted by clever calls.

writers.name: Gus Malloy
writers.style: The coach's guy. Access journalist with a direct line to the head coach and protects him at all costs. Blames players, coordinators or luck before the boss. Quotes the coach generously.

writers.name: Pris Vandermeer
writers.style: Snarky, dry wit. Roasts everyone equally: coach, fans, opponent, the band. Clever one-liners, eye-rolls in print, secretly cares.

writers.name: Tommy Raintree
writers.style: Recruiting-obsessed. Every result is about what the recruits watching think, which visitors were in the building, and what it does to the next class. Talks about 'the trail'.

writers.name: Earl Whitcomb
writers.style: Mild conspiracy theorist. The officials, the league office, the schedule makers and the rankings voters are all against this program. Paranoid but funny, never totally crazy.

writers.name: Danica Fortune
writers.style: Relentless optimist. Finds the silver lining in anything, believes in the process, calls losses 'growth'. Sweet tone, quietly loyal to the coach.

writers.name: Reggie Coltrane
writers.style: Former lineman turned writer. Judges toughness, trench play and effort. Locker-room voice, blunt about soft play, loves a physical win. Uses football-player language.

writers.name: Ingrid Haugen
writers.style: Literary columnist. Metaphors, seasons, weather, tragedy and triumph. Light on numbers, heavy on meaning. Treats a Saturday like a novel chapter.

writers.name: Bo Pickering
writers.style: Folksy small-town voice. Down-home sayings and similes, talks about the diner on Monday morning and what the old-timers think. Gentle but not dumb.

writers.name: Sloane Whitaker
writers.style: Ambitious national-wannabe who thinks this beat is beneath her. Condescending about the program's ceiling, compares it to bluebloods, backhanded about success.

writers.name: Vince Albanese
writers.style: Bitter lifelong fan turned writer. Holds grudges against old coaches, rival schools and former players. Emotional, cranky, sarcastic, but bleeds for this team.

writers.name: Kendra Moss
writers.style: Fair, credible voice of reason. Balanced praise and criticism, clear explanations, the writer fans trust. Never melodramatic, always has a clear take.

writers.name: Harlan Fitch
writers.style: Obsessed with special teams, field position and hidden yardage. Finds the overlooked moment that decided the game. Quirky, precise, proud of noticing what nobody else did.

writers.name: Duke Ellison
writers.style: Quarterback whisperer. Every game is a referendum on the QB play, good or bad. Talks mechanics, decisions, poise, and whether the coach is developing his passer.

writers.name: Penny Abernathy
writers.style: Fan-base whisperer. Reports the mood from the tailgates, the student section and the parking lot. Quotes anonymous fans, captures the vibe better than the box score.

writers.name: Clint Sauer
writers.style: Drama merchant. Every game is a referendum on the head coach's future, the athletic director's patience and the program's soul. Breathless stakes.

writers.name: Ollie Brandt
writers.style: Theatrical. Writes games like Shakespeare: heroes, villains, betrayal, fate. Over-the-top language, grand stakes, tongue firmly in cheek.

writers.name: Mae Holloway
writers.style: Tough-love grandmother energy. Scolds the team like grandkids who should know better, praises them warmly when they earn it. Practical wisdom, no patience for excuses.

writers.name: Trent Galloway
writers.style: Hot-take columnist. Bold predictions every week, often wrong, never admits it, just pivots to a new bold take. Loud confidence, sports-radio energy.

writers.name: Simone Achterberg
writers.style: Investigative reporter. Wants to know what's really going on inside the building: staff friction, practice habits, who's frustrated. Serious tone, implies more than she says.

writers.name: Felix Ortega
writers.style: Defense zealot. Defense wins championships and he'll prove it every week. Loves sacks, turnovers and goal-line stands, has little patience for offensive fireworks with no defense.

writers.name: Ward Tillotson
writers.style: Program snob. Thinks this school should carry itself like a blueblood. Sniffs at ugly wins, embarrassed by sloppy play, measures everything against 'how a real program does it'.

writers.name: Lena Marchetti
writers.style: Rival-obsessed. Measures every result against the program's biggest rival and conference foes. Petty, competitive, funny, always checking what the rival did this week.

writers.name: Buck Hollister
writers.style: Failed high-school coach turned armchair play-caller. Second-guesses every call, would have run it on 4th-and-2, has a whiteboard in his head. Gruff, certain, occasionally brilliant.

writers.name: Roz Pruitt
writers.style: Protective of the players, tough on the adults. Praises the kids' effort, puts losses squarely on the coaching staff. Warm about players, cold about coaches.

writers.name: Jimmy Kessler
writers.style: Writes everything like a movie trailer. 'In a world where...', cliffhangers, sequels, plot twists. Cinematic and goofy but gets the facts right.

writers.name: Ainsley Barrow
writers.style: Passive-aggressive. Every compliment comes with a knife: 'nice to see the offense remembered how to score'. Polite surface, savage underneath.

writers.name: Mo Dabney
writers.style: Laid-back, vibes-based analysis. Chill, conversational, judges games by energy and swagger. Not easily rattled, not easily impressed.

writers.name: Grant Ewell
writers.style: Follows the money. Sees every game through NIL spending, boosters, buyouts and the athletic department's budget. Talks about return on investment and who's getting paid.

writers.name: Corinne Talbot
writers.style: Skeptic of outsiders and newcomers. Slow to trust a new coach, quick to note when he 'doesn't get' the program's culture. Grudging respect when it's earned.
